title: Hybrid quant calibration and affine layer compensation to reduce model-specific outlier regressions
creator: Aisha R. Patel
description: Problem: After switching several models to INT8/FP8 variants we observe sporadic per-layer accuracy regressions that are model-specific (LLama v2 13B, Mistral 7B, Qwen 7B). Root cause appears correlated with high-magnitude activation outliers in specific transformer layers and uneven layer-wise scale factors during post-training quantization. Goal: Implement a hybrid calibration workflow that combines per-layer outlier-aware clipping, affine compensation (layer-wise bias/scale correction), and a light-weight validation harness to surface regressions before rollout to runtime profiles. Deliver a repeatable pipeline, a set of per-model profiles, and runtime guardrails to degrade to safer kernels if stability thresholds fail.
acceptance_criteria: Calibration pipeline runs end-to-end and outputs a per-model quant profile (FP8/INT8) stored in model-catalog for LLama/Mistral/Qwen variants.
Accuracy regression on standard validation suite is <= 0.5% relative to FP16 baseline across text-completion and chat eval sets.
Latency change for dedicated inference kernel <= 3% for typical seq_len=1024 workloads; memory footprint within 10% of current INT8 baseline.
Runtime fallback policy implemented: if model variant fails the lightweight on-deploy validation or per-route quality checks, traffic is routed to verified safe variant and incident is logged.
Documentation and runbook describing calibration steps, knobs, and how to add a new model profile.
Experiment artifacts, metrics, and PRs linked in ticket.
experiment_results: LLama-13B INT8 baseline produced avg perplexity +2.1% -> after outlier clipping + affine compensation reduced to +0.18% (vs FP16)
Mistral-7B FP8 candidate: throughput unchanged, token-latency +1.6%; accuracy delta +0.23%
Qwen-7B INT8 with per-head clamp: reduced tail-loss cases from 12/10k to 1/10k; validation BLEU/QA metrics within 0.3% of FP16
KV cache behavior verified: no cache corruption observed across repeated prefix queries (100k sequences) with affine compensation enabled
Edge-case: Mistral layer 18 required a larger clamp threshold (factor 1.8) and per-layer bias correction to remove a 0.9% regression seen on prompt-anchored completions.
decisions: Do hybrid calibration (combine global per-tensor scale estimation + per-layer outlier-aware clipping) rather than purely aggressive clipping to avoid quality loss on rare tokens.
Add small affine compensation per layer (scale+bias) stored with quant profile to correct systematic drift introduced by asymmetric quant ops.
Keep runtime kernels backward-compatible: compensation applied in load path; kernel fallbacks to safe FP16/INT8 reference if per-request validation fails.
Defer full per-head quantization pilot until post-launch: focus now on per-layer and per-head-clamping heuristics only.
tasks: Implement calibration harness that computes per-layer activation histograms, extreme-percentile stats, and candidate clamp thresholds (Marco)
Prototype affine compensation: small per-layer scale/bias estimation routine and API to persist with model profile (Aisha)
Integrate lightweight on-deploy validation (10k short prompts) into CI/CD to gate model profile rollouts (SRE)
Run A/B experiments on dedicated infra for LLama/Mistral/Qwen families and capture cost/latency/accuracy (DataEng)
Write runbook and docs for adding new model to the hybrid calibration pipeline (DOCS)
Add observability: per-profile regression alerting in Console and a debug view for per-layer activation distributions (Observability)
Open PRs and request perf/regression review; coordinate with research for tuning heuristics (Marco & Aisha)
Schedule canary rollout plan and rollback criteria with Product (PM)
